newsitem.title: DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: Dominican president may have been bomb target.
newsitem.headline: Dominican president may have been bomb target.

text.p: Dominican government officals said on Wednesday they were investigating the discovery of an explosive device apparently targeted at President Leonel Fernandez.

The device, the exact nature of which was not disclosed, was hidden at an historical site at which the president was scheduled to lay a wreath last Thursday, the 153rd anniversary of the Dominican Republic's independence.

Intelligence sources told Reuters that at least two soldiers were under investigation. But they said Fernandez's life was never in danger because the device was discovered before he arrived at Independence Park in central Santo Domingo.
Fernandez has made several public appearances since then and there was no discernible change in his security arrangements or travel plans.

Fernandez, 43, the first member of the Dominican Liberation Party elected president, was inaugurated in August 1996 and began a programme of political and economic reforms largely frustrated by the national congress, which is dominated by opposition parties.
